buckets.A: Already refused by an existing check
buckets.B: Preventable from a header field our readers can see
buckets.B2: Preventable only by a coarse policy on a PDF's contents
buckets.C: Needs decoding to detect; out of this library's reach by design
buckets.N: Not reached by opening a file
buckets.U: A reserved CVE with no text yet

reached_by.open: by opening or reading a file
reached_by.save: on a save or encode path
reached_by.api: through a call beyond opening, such as a filter or transform
reached_by.tool: through a command-line tool, not the library
reached_by.other: some other way; the finding says

records.title: A FlashPix file runs code when opened, if olefile is installed
records.summary: Heap buffer overflow in FlashPix (FPX) JPEG-tile decoding leads to code execution.
records.trigger: A single crafted FlashPix file, recognised by its OLE2 bytes, opened with Image.open() on an installation with the optional olefile package.
records.finding: OLE (which carries FlashPix and old Office files) is refused by name from the first bytes.

refusal.setting: OLE is refused whatever the policy says

protect.general: Upgrade to Pillow 13.0.0. Do not install olefile where it is not needed.
protect.specific: formats=[...] on Image.open, or sillybos in front of it.

records.notes: Bounded, not closed: the limit turns an unbounded cost into a bounded one.
records.title: A PNG's EXIF chunk makes parsing take quadratic time
records.summary: A PNG eXIf chunk full of repeated six-byte markers makes Exif.load() copy the buffer once per marker.
records.trigger: Opening a PNG and reading its EXIF (getexif()) when the eXIf chunk is large and filled with repeated markers. The advisory says a photo-sized file is enough.
records.finding: The size of every PNG chunk other than image data is read before decoding and held to max_metadata_bytes (4 MiB by default, 1 MiB strict). That bounds the cost; it does not remove it, since a chunk under the limit still costs seconds.

refusal.setting: lower max_metadata_bytes for files from outside

protect.specific: Cap metadata blocks well below what a scan carries (kilobytes): sillybos --max-metadata-bytes.

records.title: A multi-frame file that changes colour mode writes into a buffer sized for the first frame
records.summary: Multi-frame loaders can reuse stale native image storage after a mode transition, giving out-of-bounds writes; command execution was demonstrated through the MPO path.
records.trigger: Iterating the frames of a crafted multi-picture JPEG (MPO), TIFF or Photoshop file whose later frame is a wider colour mode than the first.
records.finding: Every frame of a TIFF and every picture of a multi-picture JPEG is read and required to match the first in colour mode, samples and bit depth; a file that changes is refused. Photoshop files are refused by format.

refusal.setting: no setting: a frame that differs from the first is always a refusal

protect.specific: Require every frame of a multi-frame file to share the first frame's mode and size before decoding; sillybos does.

records.title: A SPIDER stack file bypasses the pixel limit on seek
records.summary: SpiderImagePlugin's seek() re-parses the header without the decompression-bomb check, so a file under 1 KB can trigger a multi-gigabyte allocation.
records.trigger: Opening a crafted SPIDER file and loading a later frame.
records.finding: SPIDER is not a format the check knows, so the file is refused as an unknown format before any reader runs.

refusal.setting: unknown formats are refused whatever the policy says

protect.specific: Allow-list the formats you mean to read; everything else, including this one, never reaches a reader.

records.title: A later frame of an MPO or DCX file is never checked against the pixel limit
records.summary: The decompression-bomb check runs only on the first frame; MpoImageFile.seek() and DcxImageFile.seek() do not repeat it.
records.trigger: Seeking to a later frame of a multi-picture JPEG, or a DCX file, whose first frame is tiny and whose later frame declares enormous dimensions.
records.finding: Every picture of a multi-picture JPEG is read from the index and each held to max_pixels. DCX is not a known format and is refused as unknown.

refusal.setting: applied to every picture, not the first

protect.specific: Apply the pixel limit to every frame, not the first; sillybos does.

records.title: A 512-byte XBM file stalls Image.open() for minutes
records.summary: A regular expression in XbmImagePlugin takes about six minutes of CPU on a crafted 512-byte file before Image.open() gives up.
records.trigger: Opening a crafted file that looks enough like an XBM for Pillow to try its XBM reader.
records.finding: XBM is not a format the check knows, so the file is refused as an unknown format; with formats=[...] set, Pillow never tries the XBM reader either.

refusal.setting: unknown formats are refused whatever the policy says

protect.specific: Allow-list the formats you mean to read.

records.title: An EPS file's name is passed to Ghostscript as an option
records.summary: Argument injection in the Ghostscript call, potentially leading to remote code execution.
records.trigger: Opening an EPS (PostScript) file, recognised by content whatever its name, when Ghostscript is installed; the file's own name is read as a Ghostscript option.
records.finding: PostScript is not one of the four formats and is refused by name from the first bytes, so no PostScript file reaches Pillow's EPS reader through the check.

refusal.setting: PostScript is refused whatever the policy says

protect.general: Upgrade to Pillow 13.0.0. Do not install Ghostscript on a machine that opens files from outside unless it is needed.
protect.specific: Image.open(path, formats=["JPEG", "PNG", "TIFF"]) keeps the EPS reader from ever running; sillybos refuses the file before that.

records.title: An animated PNG allocates its full canvas before the pixel limit is checked
records.summary: APNG background disposal allocates the full canvas before the decompression-bomb check; a 126-byte file claiming 22,000 x 22,000 pixels costs about 1.9 GB.
records.trigger: Opening a small animated PNG whose IHDR claims enormous dimensions.
records.finding: Width and height are read from the IHDR, and the frame count from acTL, before any decoder runs; the product is held to max_pixels and the count to max_pages.

refusal.setting: from the header, before Pillow allocates

protect.specific: Read the declared size from the header and refuse before the decoder allocates; sillybos does.

records.title: Saving a TIFF to memory overruns a heap buffer
records.summary: Heap buffer overflow in _tiffWriteProc when saving TIFF to BytesIO.
records.trigger: Saving any image as TIFF to an in-memory destination (io.BytesIO) rather than a file; the data written past the buffer is attacker-chosen when the image came from outside.
records.finding: A save-path flaw. Nothing read from the incoming file's header decides it, so a check before decoding cannot reach it.

protect.general: Upgrade to Pillow 13.0.0. Until then, save TIFFs to a file on disk, not to memory.
protect.specific: Not something a pre-decode check can prevent; listed so that nobody expects it to.

records.title: Pillow's PDF parser recurses without limit when appending
records.summary: PdfParser can recurse without limit in get_value() and linearize_page_tree().
records.trigger: Image.save(..., format="PDF", append=True) onto an attacker-controlled existing PDF.
records.finding: Reached only through Pillow's PDF append path, which Image.open never runs.

protect.general: Upgrade to Pillow 13.0.0. Do not append to PDFs you did not make.
protect.specific: Not a pre-decode matter.

records.title: A MIC file makes counting its frames loop for ever
records.summary: Infinite loop in MIC n_frames when the embedded TIFF has three or more directories; needs the optional olefile package.
records.trigger: Opening a crafted MIC (Microsoft Image Composer) file, an OLE container, and reading n_frames.
records.finding: OLE is refused by name from the first bytes.

refusal.setting: OLE is refused whatever the policy says

protect.general: Upgrade to Pillow 13.0.0. Do not install olefile where it is not needed.
protect.specific: formats=[...] on Image.open, or sillybos in front of it.

records.title: A malformed compressed TIFF leaks heap memory into its pixels
records.summary: Out-of-bounds read in TiffDecode.c tile and RGBA paths copies heap memory into the returned image.
records.trigger: Opening and loading a malformed compressed TIFF; the returned pixels carry fragments of the process's memory, which a service that returns thumbnails hands back.
records.finding: The tiled path is refused under the strict preset; the RGBA path is not something the header distinguishes, so this is only partly within reach.

refusal.setting: STRICT, or Policy(allow_tiled_tiff=False); the RGBA path is not covered

protect.general: Upgrade to Pillow 13.0.0. Never return pixels decoded from an untrusted file without re-encoding them first.
protect.specific: Refuse tiled TIFFs where scans are striped; keep the decoder current for the rest.

records.title: A lossless JPEG overruns the decode buffer when scaled
records.summary: Heap buffer overflow in ImagingJpegDecode: a lossless (SOF3) frame ignores the requested scaling and writes full-width rows into a buffer sized for the scaled width.
records.trigger: A standards-compliant lossless JPEG, opened and then drafted or thumbnailed (Image.thumbnail() does this on its own). The advisory notes that formats=["JPEG"] does not prevent it.
records.finding: The frame coding is read from the JPEG's frame header. The default policy allows baseline, extended and progressive frames only; a lossless frame is refused with the coding named.

refusal.setting: jpeg_frames excludes lossless by default

protect.general: Upgrade to Pillow 13.0.0. Call load() before thumbnail(), or pass reducing_gap=None, until then.
protect.specific: Refuse frame codings a scanner never writes: lossless, hierarchical, arithmetic. sillybos does this by default.

records.title: A tiled TIFF makes the decoder read past its tile buffer
records.summary: The tiled-TIFF decoder reads past the tile buffer in copy4 when libtiff returns a tile smaller than the worst case.
records.trigger: Opening and loading a malformed tiled TIFF.
records.finding: Whether a TIFF is tiled is in its directory. The default policy allows tiles (digitisation and mapping software write them) and holds each tile to max_pixels; the strict preset refuses tiled TIFFs outright.

refusal.setting: STRICT, or Policy(allow_tiled_tiff=False)

protect.specific: If your scans are striped, not tiled, refuse tiled TIFFs: sillybos --no-tiled-tiff, or the strict preset.

records.title: A PixarLog-compressed TIFF overflows a libtiff heap buffer
records.summary: Decoding a PixarLog image with the 8-bit ABGR output format and a specific stride leads to a heap-based buffer overflow.
records.affected: libtiff, as packaged; see the upstream record
records.trigger: Opening a TIFF compressed with PixarLog.
records.finding: The compression scheme is a directory tag. The default policy allows none, CCITT, LZW, JPEG, Deflate and PackBits; PixarLog and the other codecs a scan never uses are refused by name.

refusal.setting: tiff_compressions excludes PixarLog by default

protect.specific: Allow only the compression schemes your files use; sillybos --tiff-compressions.

records.notes: Cited from the policy's own notes (policy.py), written from the advisory at the time; the OSV record was unreachable when this entry was made and its fields should be filled in.
records.title: A palette PNG reaches a flaw in libpng's palette handling
records.summary: One of three libpng flaws in the paths that handle palette (indexed-colour) PNGs. The upstream record was not re-fetched when this entry was written; see notes.
records.trigger: Opening a palette-type PNG.
records.finding: The colour type is in the PNG's IHDR. The default allows all five colour types; a policy for scans alone can keep to greyscale and RGB, which keeps palette PNGs from the decoder.

refusal.setting: Policy(png_colour_types={"greyscale", "rgb"})

protect.specific: If nothing you handle is a palette PNG, say so in the policy: sillybos --png-colour-types greyscale,rgb.

records.title: A YCbCr TIFF subsampled four to one overflows a libtiff buffer
records.summary: Signed integer overflow in putcontig8bitYCbCr44tile leads to an out-of-bounds heap write.
records.affected: libtiff, as packaged; see the upstream record
records.trigger: Opening a YCbCr TIFF whose chroma subsampling is 4x4, through the RGBA reading path.
records.finding: A YCbCr TIFF's subsampling is a directory tag. The default policy allows 1x1, 2x1, 1x2 and 2x2, which is what scanners and cameras write; 4x4 and the other factor-of-four values are refused.

refusal.setting: tiff_subsamplings excludes factor-of-four by default

protect.specific: Allow only the subsamplings your files use; sillybos --tiff-subsamplings.

records.notes: Cited from the policy's own notes (policy.py); the OSV record was unreachable when this entry was made and its fields should be filled in.
records.title: An interlaced 16-bit PNG overflows a libpng buffer
records.summary: One of two libpng overflows on the Adam7-interlaced 16-bit path. The upstream record was not re-fetched when this entry was written; see notes.
records.trigger: Opening an Adam7-interlaced PNG with 16-bit samples.
records.finding: Interlacing is in the IHDR. No scanner writes an interlaced PNG, so the default refuses one.

refusal.setting: allow_interlaced_png is off by default

protect.specific: Refuse interlaced PNGs; nothing that scans a page writes one. sillybos does by default.

records.notes: Cited from the policy's own notes (policy.py), written from the advisory at the time; the OSV record was unreachable when this entry was made and its fields should be filled in.

records.title: An abnormally tall TIFF makes libtiff write colour data to an arbitrary address
records.summary: A flaw was found in Libtiff.
records.affected: LibTIFF, as packaged; see the upstream record
records.trigger: Reading a TIFF whose image height is abnormally large, through libtiff's RGBA image reading.
records.finding: The height is in the first directory, which sillybos reads. A height large enough to carry the pixel count past max_pixels was already refused; a tall, narrow image within the pixel budget was not, until max_side: every page, frame and tile is now held to it on its longest side (30,000 by default; no scanner writes a side longer than a few tens of thousands of pixels).

refusal.setting: max_side

protect.general: Upgrade libtiff to a version that has the fix; the upstream record names it.
protect.specific: Set max_side from your corpus (the longest side of your largest real page, times two or three); sillybos refuses a taller or wider image before libtiff sees it.

records.notes: Proposed from the advisory's text on 2026-11-01, as part of folding the backfill into the record; not yet confirmed by a person.

records.title: A TIFF tag that points past the file makes libtiff allocate for nothing
records.summary: An out-of-memory flaw in libtiff: a crafted file passed to TIFFOpen() makes it allocate from a tag's declared size.
records.trigger: Opening a TIFF whose directory declares a tag with a count that puts its data beyond the end of the file.
records.finding: Every tag's out-of-line data is checked to lie inside the file before anything decodes, and the largest block is held to max_metadata_bytes.

refusal.setting: and the tag-inside-the-file check, which has no setting

protect.general: Keep libtiff current; it is the TIFF reader under Pillow, poppler and most of the rest.
protect.specific: Check tag offsets and sizes against the file size before opening; sillybos does.
